paper.title: Minimum Distance Summaries for Robust Neural Posterior Estimation

challenge_claims_exact.text: Minimum-distance summaries provide a plug-in robust neural posterior estimation method that adapts test-time summaries independently of pretrained NPE using maximum mean discrepancy.
The algorithm is implemented efficiently with random Fourier feature approximations, yielding a lightweight, model-free test-time adaptation procedure.
The method demonstrates substantial robustness gains with minimal additional overhead.
Theoretical guarantees for the robustness of the algorithm are provided.

claims.title: Frozen plug-in separation
claims.paper_scope: MDS adapts the query summary at test time while keeping the pretrained NPE fixed.
claims.result: Frozen posterior hashes and 550 paired adaptations preserve the offline NPE while changing only the test-time summary.
claims.limitation: The evidence covers the recorded Gaussian and OUP mechanisms, not every paper task.

claims.title: RFF/MSE/L-BFGS implementation
claims.paper_scope: MDS uses Gaussian-kernel MMD, random Fourier features, an MSE-trained decoder embedding, and test-time L-BFGS.
claims.result: The pinned official RFF path, strong-Wolfe L-BFGS signatures, CPU timing, and exact-versus-RFF comparisons pass.
claims.limitation: The official repository default is 256 RFFs; this reproduction explicitly uses the paper's 512-RFF setting.

claims.title: Theorem 4.1 robustness bound
claims.paper_scope: Under Appendix A.1 assumptions, the posterior-KL influence bound is finite.
claims.result: All ten printed assumptions pass, but a zero target Hessian creates a quartically flat objective; KL divided by contamination diverges.
claims.limitation: This is an exact counterexample to the universal statement, not a claim that all practical MDS objectives are flat.

claims.title: Theorem 4.2 consistency transfer
claims.paper_scope: Under Appendix A.3 assumptions, original-summary posterior weak consistency implies MDS-summary posterior weak consistency.
claims.result: The original posterior contracts while MDS selects an escaping point mass; bounded ISPD does not supply the stronger C0 topology needed for the claimed transfer.
claims.limitation: The result targets the theorem's universal assumptions and does not invalidate correctly specified compact or C0-controlled applications.

claims.title: Gaussian all-comparator robustness gloss
claims.paper_scope: Audit target imported from the challenge/release wording: MDS beats every named comparator below 40% contamination.
claims.result: MDS beats NPE and NNPE through 30% contamination, but NPE-OR is better at 30%: MMD 1.0626 versus 2.0756, paired 95% interval [-1.3538, -0.6719].
claims.limitation: The verdict is deliberately limited to the stronger all-comparator gloss and does not reject the paper's qualified in-general wording.

claims.title: 1024-dimensional Cryo-EM result
claims.paper_scope: The Cryo-EM experiment achieves the paper's displayed large RMSE reductions.
claims.result: The paper's vector Figure 4 reports 58–63% reductions, while one exact-scale retraining reports 2.8–8.5%; four routes do not establish a defensible final verdict.
claims.limitation: The authors' exact checkpoint and Figure 4 training/test data realization are unavailable.
